Question: Can you write a short story with two meanings?
Answer: Black shirt, unkept hair, a staunch aroma and a cotton trouser that hadn’t touched detergents in ages adorned a man sitting quietly on the bench outside the bar. The year was 1958, and he had just left everything he owned behind. 11 years since Independence, and he was still unheard of. His sense of pride and freedom was entangled, he spoke only when spoken to. He had a missing thumb on his right hand, a broken nasal septum and a golden molar teeth. He had all the money in the world but his scars from the prisoner camp made him feel poor. The government had earmarked him for a covert operation in Baluchistan years ago, and because of him a lot of intel poured in during the 1948 war. Now, he was just a mismatch in the society. He had seen war, he had seen people on both sides of the border before and after partition. His fluent Urdu and Punjabi had helped him survive his espionage. He sat outside the bar in Calcutta waiting for a weapons dealer from East Pakistan. His family had been burnt alive in Mathura and his only friend was now a cabinet minister in the government. For what was worth, his only friend was his denial of government policies on both sides of the border. He had realised it on day one of his espionage that everything was about gaining power and sitting on the chair eventually during a war, even if it is only for a few days, and that is why he enjoyed lonely benches. A tall man walked out wearing a grey overcoat. His hair was greyish with a tinge of brown that reeked of poor quality Henna. He stood up from the bench and took out his Beretta, paused for a while, took a deep breathe and felt the trigger hard enough to penetrate the weapons dealer’s spine. There was no one around and the live band inside the bar was too loud. He walked away staring at the dead man on the pavement. Another man down, another propaganda by a government successfully propagated and another sin encumbered on an assassin’s soul. For years, people like him have been trained and kept undercover to carry out such minuscule operations. The reward is nullified absence of conscience in such young men. Governments on both sides of the border emulate the same. Israel, USA, Russia, even African nations have a pool of such men whom nobody has heard of. By the time, they taste their first kill, they all realise the truth. It is all about who will be in power when the elections come. Black hoodie, a white underlying tee and a torn jeans that talked about his stint in Belarus decorated a man who was sitting just outside Sonagachi in Kolkatta. Everywhere, there were posters of the state’s leaders. The man was silently waiting for a booth capturer from Bangladesh. Elections were coming again and this time there was a new propaganda. The year was 2019.

Question: How can I sign up myself for a triathlon, and what are the selection processes for it?
Answer: Thanks for the question, I will purely it answer in the Indian context. Firstly, a Triathlon has 3 legs - Swim, Cycle, and then run. It has become popular of late in India as well, as it is considered the ultimate test of your endurance, stamina and discipline in life. There are 4 official distances that are recognized worldwide: If you are looking to start off with triathlons, you should ideally start off with Sprint or Olympic distances. In India, there are quite a few organizations that organize triathlons for everyone to participate, but there are no selection criteria as such. Anyone above 18 years can participate as long as they pay the participation fees. Basic gear requirements: Swimming cap, goggles, cycle (preferably road or TT), helmet, running shoes, cycling and running clothes or a triathlon suit. Ironman Goa 70.3 - This is an annual event that takes place in Goa, sponsored by Ironman (a global triathlon brand). The fee is around 40,000 INR and the cut-off time is 8 hours 30 minutes. The event is perfectly organised and the standards are really upto the mark. It is the benchmark for triathlon races around the world. Finishing it in time is considered a huge achievement. If you can financially sustain, you can also choose to go outside India, and participate in Ironman events across the world. Bergman 113 - This is the Indian version of Ironman (70.3 miles is 113 kms). Takes place in Kolhapur and Pune every year. They have Sprint, Olympic, and 70.3 distances. Participation fees are around 13,000 for 70.3 distance. This is also well organised and I would recommend this to anyone who is looking to experience Triathlons in India. Herculean Tri - Another organization that organizes Triathlons in Udaipur and Konark. Only one which features a full distance (140.6) race in India. They also have 70. distance and Olympic distance. I have not attended this event. KSC Tri - This is a small-scale triathlon event in Kolhapur event which happens annually, organised by Kolhapur Sports Club. It is very friendly and cut off time is around 9 hours for 70.3 so it is quite relaxed. Participation fees is around 8,000. There are a few more that are organized like BMF Tri in Bengaluru, Tuffman in Chandigarh, and NEB in Malpe Beach. The gold level of all of these would be Ironman Goa 70.3 always. Sharing Links to all of these here: Please note most events happen from August to October. Ironman Goa 70.3 - Bergman 113 - Herculean Tri - BMF Triathlon - NEB 113 - To complete a 70.3 distance (1.9k swim, 90k bike, 21.1 run), you will need at least 6 months of training and preparation depending on your current fitness state. Start off with a sprint or Olympic distance and see how you fare first. Open to more queries and opinions in the comments, and open to coaching new triathletes as well. [1]

Question: Defence aspirants please answer me honestly, is SSB that tough or it is overhyped by the ones who didn’t clear it?
Answer: I was catching up with a dear coursemate who is now a GTO. We were reminiscing about our younger days and how our SSB experience was. We both had cleared it in the first attempt during our 12th standard. One thing he pointed out about the present lot of candidates hit me really hard. “Things have changed a lot. We had no distractions back then. When I was giving my SSB, there were not many online videos or portals trying to preach about the techniques. We just read about the process, exercised regularly and were ourselves. Nowadays, everyone has access to so much SSB content everywhere, and each with different techniques that these candidates are like a monkey with knowledge they don’t know what to do. I have seen people memorise their cliched answers like their answer to why they want to join the forces and so on. They practice the psychology tests, which is insane, it openly violates the purpose of it.” “Man, you’re so frustrated.” I laughed. “They just have to be themselves during the SSB. I don’t know why they want to show off to me all their knowledge on defence. I am a senior officer, you think I would not know that. For most of them it’s just a another opportunity when their engineering or medical seats don’t work out. I’m just irradiated by this generation of wannabe OLQ holders.” The rant went on for an hour or so. The point is, you don’t need to overhype it. Be yourself, keep it simple, and if you’re really worthy and passionate, you will be recommended. Keep it simple and remember an empty vessel makes more noise. Jai Hind!
